title: Projects
text:
Hackathons and research Statistics and analytics Software and engineering

Please reach out on LinkedIn if you want to learn more about any of these.


The Daily Grind (CMD-F 2025)Built a conversation-starter web app in 24 hours that won the Social track and placed 3rd overall out of 50+ projects.Hackathon Team project

A 24-hour hackathon with 50+ projects and 200+ participants. We built a coffee-chat conversation starter that won the Social track and placed 3rd overall. After presenting to 7 judges we were invited to present to the whole hackathon community of 250+ people.



Preview of the conversation starter. Users add details in a popup and get conversation topics.


See it on Devpost



DataFest Statistical Analysis (ASA 2025)A fully reproducible 48-hour analysis with a Bayesian model, delivered with a dashboard, demo video and slides, all in Quarto.Bayesian modelling EDA Hackathon

A 48-hour American Statistical Association DataFest project with a team of 3. We built a fully reproducible analysis with extensive EDA and a Bayesian model, and delivered a dashboard, demo video and presentation slides, all made with Quarto.
Presentation · Repository



Statistical Research Consulting (Capstone)Real client work in medical research: analyzed glaucoma surgery outcomes in R, presented at a poster session and to the client.Statistics R Consulting

Real consulting work for a client in medical research, analyzing changes after glaucoma eye surgery (STAT 450).

Presented regularly to Professor Rodolfo Lourenzutti to keep the work reliable.
Met with the client, presented findings at a poster session, and gave technical oral presentations.
Produced written reports, a code repository and visualizations in R and GitHub.
Learned a lot about study design, model selection and communicating statistics.




Our final poster board





Reproducible Software and CI/CD (DSCI 310)An R package plus an automated analysis pipeline using Docker, GNU Make and GitHub Actions, with tests and documentation.R package Docker GitHub Actions

A group project to build a data analysis and a package that are fully reproducible:

A documented, modular R package and scripts
An analysis pipeline automated with GNU Make
A reproducible report in R Markdown and Quarto
A containerized environment shared through Docker
Automated tests, documentation and deployment




Preview of the package repository


Package repository · Analysis repository



This Portfolio WebsiteA multi-page site built with Quarto and custom CSS, deployed on GitHub Pages, with a responsive layout that works on phones.Quarto CSS GitHub Pages

I designed and built this site myself. It is written in Quarto and hosted on GitHub Pages.

A custom stylesheet with a consistent palette and color-coded project tracks
A responsive layout, including a hero section, card grids and expandable project sections
Separate pages for projects, certifications and courses, with image lightboxes

Repository



Weather Extremes ResearchSummer research assistantship (URSA NSERC) using time series analysis in Python and R to find patterns in Canadian floods, droughts and wildfires.Research Time series Python

Research assistant at UBC in summer 2024 under a URSA NSERC scholarship, working with Professors Harry Joe and Natalia Nolde. I explored Canadian weather data on floods, droughts and wildfires to find patterns, using EDA and time series analysis, and presented my work weekly. I’m cleaning up the code to publish it in a public repository.



Library Attendance Dashboard (DSCI 320)An interactive Python dashboard on San Francisco library attendance, built with two teammates to answer four research questions.Python Data visualization

With two teammates, I built an interactive dashboard on library attendance in the San Francisco area. The course required inventive visualizations to answer 4 questions, and the dashboard has toggles that the image doesn’t show.



Custom dashboard for DSCI 320: Data Visualization





wordplayr, an R packageA documented R package with a vignette and a pkgdown website that finds patterns in word lists.R package Roxygen pkgdown

wordplayr finds patterns in a list of words: average word length, common starting letters, frequent vowel sounds and more. It has a README with install instructions, a vignette, a package website and Roxygen documentation. I built it to learn why I like my favorite words (they most often start with “C”).



Preview of the package website


Repository · Website



easyEDA, a Python package (in progress)A Python package that automates exploratory data analysis by choosing the right plot for each column’s data type.Python package EDA

A package that automates EDA for any dataset by picking suitable plots for each column’s data type. It supports quick exploration and presentation-ready, interactive visuals, and I plan to add an R version.

title: About
text:
I’m a data modernization consultant working toward a career in data engineering. I graduated from the University of British Columbia in May 2025 with a major in Statistics and a minor in Data Science, including a semester at the University of Oslo.
Day to day I work with Databricks, Microsoft Fabric and Power BI in Python, R, SQL and DAX. I’m interested in data engineering, Azure consulting, and analytics and experimentation roles.
My statistics background shows up in my work: I’ve done a research consulting capstone, a research assistantship in climate extremes, and hackathons where we shipped under pressure. Outside of work, I enjoy running, climbing, and crocheting.
